roles.label: Board wipe
roles.description: Broadly removes or resets multiple opposing objects.

roles.label: Card advantage
roles.description: Draws or otherwise supplies repeatable access to additional cards.

roles.label: Card selection
roles.description: Improves draw quality through scry, surveil, or top-card selection.

roles.label: Combat trick
roles.description: Changes combat math from hand or at instant speed.

roles.label: Combo piece
roles.description: Participates in a named combo or repeatable interaction package in this deck.

roles.label: Counter synergy
roles.description: Creates, multiplies, moves, or rewards counters.

roles.label: Counterspell
roles.description: Counters a spell or stack object.

roles.label: Engine
roles.description: Can generate repeatable strategic value when supported.

roles.label: Graveyard hate
roles.description: Constrains, exiles, or otherwise disrupts graveyard use.

roles.label: Land synergy
roles.description: Enables or rewards the deck's land, land-type, Gate, Locus, or landfall plan.

roles.label: Lifegain
roles.description: Gains life or grants a repeatable lifegain mechanism.

roles.label: Lifegain payoff
roles.description: Rewards life gain or a high life total.

roles.label: Protection
roles.description: Protects a card, board, or line from opposing interaction.

roles.label: Ramp
roles.description: Accelerates usable mana beyond ordinary one-land-per-turn development.

roles.label: Recursion
roles.description: Returns, casts, or plays cards from a graveyard.

roles.label: Removal
roles.description: Answers a permanent, creature, or other opposing game object.

roles.label: Sacrifice outlet
roles.description: Lets its controller deliberately sacrifice another relevant permanent.

roles.label: Token production
roles.description: Creates creature or relevant resource tokens.

roles.label: Tutor
roles.description: Searches the library for one or more strategically selected cards.

roles.label: Win condition
roles.description: Represents a primary or explicit route by which this deck can end a game.

notes.text: Deploy this before a sequence of separate life-gain events; its main value is efficient scaling that turns incidental gains into a credible attacker.
Plan this reset in advance: extract value from expendable artifacts first and retain a planeswalker, land, or recursion line that rebuilds better than the table.
Choose the mode that serves the board: fabricate bodies for extort, sacrifice, and anthem value, or counters when one resilient evasive threat is preferable.
Play this before multiple small life-gain events when possible; the extra life accelerates the deck's threshold payoffs without creating additional triggers.
Place this on a creature that converts evasion and first strike into meaningful pressure, with preference for a commander-damage or double-strike line.
Use Arvad as a compact anthem when multiple legendary attackers benefit; otherwise value the deathtouch-lifelink body as a deterrent rather than forcing combat.
Hold this flexible answer for a creature or planeswalker worth spending premium removal on; multicolored targets also advance life-total thresholds.

When an oversized Boo is the payload for Minsc & Boo's -2 ability, prefer destroying Boo over the planeswalker if the commander can be recast promptly. Removing the Hamster prevents both its power-sized damage and the associated card draw, whereas removing only Minsc may leave the payload ready for the recast.
Keep this available as protection when an important creature is exposed; once safety is secured, its power and evasion can support a decisive attack.
Sequence this tapped accelerator on a turn that does not sacrifice interaction or a stronger development play, then use it to reach black-heavy payoffs.
Use this as premium untapped color fixing, preserving narrower or painful sources for turns when their special qualities matter.
Treat this as a steady bridge: above the starting total it draws cards, while at or below that total it helps climb back toward the deck's life thresholds.

Against repeatable legendary-token threats such as Boo, treat Darksteel Mutation as tempo rather than permanent removal: the controller can create a new legendary copy, choose the enchanted token to leave under the legend rule, and strand the Aura. Cast it when the immediate prevention of attacks or token-based value justifies that temporary window.
Establish this before repeatable life gain, but reserve mana selectively; pay for cards when they improve the plan and make Soldiers when bodies have immediate utility.
Use this after a meaningful attacker or activated creature becomes tapped, gaining life while removing a target that justifies the narrow timing window.
Scale this to remove an essential target or close a life race; large casts are best when the gained life also activates threshold or drain payoffs.
Treat this as a multiplayer finisher and life-reset tool; bank mana and pair it with life-gain payoffs rather than spending it for a modest early swing.
Deploy this before meaningful life gain when it can survive; its drain scales with the amount gained, while separate gains add targeting flexibility and trigger other event-count payoffs.
Preserve convoke bodies and white mana to represent this during combat, prioritizing an attacker or blocker whose exile changes the outcome materially.
Tutor for the missing function—mana, draw, protection, interaction, payoff, or finisher—rather than defaulting to the most expensive threat.
Accumulate counters through separate gains, then treat its death as stored board presence; temporary power boosts can enlarge the resulting token recovery.
Sequence life gain before combat to cross Elenda's power and evasion thresholds, then protect or enable her when commander damage offers the cleanest route.
Grow this before exposing it to combat; its counters remain strategic capital because death can transfer them onto the creature best positioned to use them.
Arrange at least one counter event on different turns, including opponents' turns when possible, to turn its once-per-turn draw ceiling into sustained advantage.
Save this scalable drain for a life reset or finishing turn, especially when other permanents convert the single large gain into additional damage or counters.
Use this for early acceleration when opponents supply the needed color, but verify its live colors before planning a tightly colored follow-up.
Build its power before cashing it in so the death trigger can recover a better creature; choose a non-Bear target that restores the most useful engine link.
Use this when the temporary power and lifelink create a threshold, profitable combat, or larger death payoff rather than as an incidental damage boost.
Treat the land face as needed for early color development; cast the Aura only when flying and lifelink create a materially stronger combat or life-gain line.
Prioritize one consequential permanent from each opponent and protect the enchantment when possible, since losing it returns every exiled resource.
Use this as an inexpensive source of separate life-gain events and early evasive pressure, not as a creature that must be preserved at all costs.
Keep this unconditional creature-or-planeswalker answer for a target that threatens immediate advantage or blocks the deck's planned turn.
Make opponents account for this deterrent; protection or indestructibility can turn damage into removal without sacrificing the Priest.
Choose the opponent least able to spare creatures or life, and expect the table to deny cards when the alternative cost is inexpensive.
Use this as low-risk glue: it replaces itself, creates a life-gain event, and leaves an evasive body for pressure, convoke, or sacrifice.
Sequence desired reanimation before deploying this graveyard lock; afterward use its vigilance, menace, and lifelink to stabilize without disabling your own next line unexpectedly.
Value an opening-hand copy highly, then leverage its replacement effect to reach the anthem threshold; remember it increases amounts, not the number of gain events.

Bank petal counters until they enable a meaningful double-spell or X-spell turn. Because unspent mana empties at phase boundaries, sacrifice Lotus Blossom during the response window to the first main-phase spell, then spend the floating mana after that spell resolves.
Deploy Lyra when her anthem and shared lifelink improve multiple Angels, or when the first-strike body can safely stabilize an otherwise dangerous combat.
Play this before repeated small life-gain events; each event drains every opponent, making event count more important than raw amount.
Sequence this tapped accelerator on an otherwise quiet turn so later white requirements do not compete with deploying the deck's four-mana engines.
Attack when safe to bank Food, then preserve the enchantment until a large life-gain turn makes its sacrifice a meaningful finishing threat.
Choose X according to tempo, then use Mikaeus either as a renewable counter source or as a wide-board pump when several creatures can exploit it.
Use this efficiently against a small utility creature or to alter combat, with the life gain serving as an additional trigger rather than the sole reason to cast it.
Spend this clean creature answer on a target whose continued presence outweighs the value of holding instant-speed interaction for a later threat.
Favor high-toughness targets so the enters trigger both removes a real threat and produces a substantial life swing; recursion can reuse that exchange.
Cast this cheaply when an evasive lifelinker matters, but hold it for kicker when returning a high-impact creature is worth the slower tempo.
Use this as early fixing that also supplies a distinct life-gain event; later it remains a disposable artifact creature for Trading Post lines.
Deploy this early to turn spare generic mana into both deck colors, but account for its activation cost when planning exact sequencing.
Place this on a creature likely to attack elsewhere, using goad for political pressure while its repeated drain advances your life thresholds.
Resolve this when the life payment is comfortably supported; its steady cards are strongest before the hand runs dry, not after tempo has already collapsed.
Treat basic Plains as dependable untapped white development and a resilient target for basic-land search effects.
Deploy this before opponents' ramp or land-heavy turns; the repeated independent gains fuel event-based payoffs while taxing ordinary development.
Build a creature count and retain cheap follow-up spells before casting Pontiff; each other creature becomes another extort trigger and a potential mass-drain engine.
Use flash to answer the most consequential nonland permanent at the latest safe moment, gaining life while preserving main-phase development.
Tap this at the latest safe point before your next untap when the mana would otherwise go unused, turning one activation per untap cycle into a separate life-gain event.

Reserve this for a creature whose immediate recovery value justifies the current mana cost. Check whether a discount is actually available, and preserve colored mana for any extort payments before committing the spell.
Use its attack trigger to cross a life threshold before blockers, but animate only when the mana commitment and exposure are justified by that swing.
Preserve this utility land for a decisive attacker; its activation is expensive enough that colored development normally comes first.
Reanimate or cast this to find the exact missing role, then reuse the enters trigger when recursion makes that more valuable than tutoring only a finisher.
Sequence this tapped dual on a low-pressure turn; its life trigger is small but still improves payoffs that count separate gain events.
Reveal a basic land when convenient to preserve tempo, but do not distort a stronger land sequence merely to make this enter untapped.
Establish this while the life total is stable or rising, then sequence white spells and protection to keep meeting its upkeep draw benchmark.
Deploy this early when the colorless burst advances a real mana threshold, while still planning enough colored sources for the deck's key spells.
Use this to fix development, then welcome a profitable block or sacrifice so the death draw converts the body into another card.

When a large lifegain spell is available, deploy Sorin before gaining the life so the transformed -1 ability can convert that turn's life gain into targeted damage. Sequence the lifegain spell before activating Sorin unless an immediate defensive activation is necessary.
Exploit the turn-wide lifelink before combat or damage abilities, and choose the reanimation value of X without sacrificing Sorin's future utility unnecessarily.
Treat basic Swamp as dependable untapped black development and a resilient target for basic-land search effects.
Use this to protect a strategically important creature or grant haste for immediate value; avoid exposing it on a low-impact body without a reason.
Use the scry to support the next mana and payoff sequence, putting low-impact cards below when the hand already covers their role.
Treat each mode as part of a resource loop: discard reanimation targets, cash in expendable artifacts or creatures, and choose the exchange that links the next play.
Deploy before life gain to grow it, then use the life threshold and temporary lifelink or power boosts to make double strike decisive.
Reserve this flexible exile effect for a nonland permanent that narrower removal cannot handle or whose recursion would make destruction inadequate.
Preserve its flexibility: protect a key creature from a removal or sweep, or remove a large threat when doing so matters more than insurance.
Use this early when a real land is preferable to a fragile rock, selecting the basic color that unlocks the next planned spells.
Choose a reanimation target for immediate impact or engine connectivity, and avoid committing it while your own graveyard lock is active.

packages.label: Lifegain/drain package
packages.description: Turns life gain and high life totals into counters, pressure, and table-wide life loss.

notes.text: Deploy this before a turn with multiple counter placements; loyalty, creature counters, proliferate, and landfall can then become removal or a direct finishing line.
Deploy this early when it advances colored development, but count it as vulnerable acceleration rather than a substitute for a stable land base.
Preserve this broad answer for a permanent that materially threatens the plan; the replacement body is usually preferable to leaving an engine or win condition intact.
Prioritize this as turn-one fixing when it accelerates Minsc, accepting that the small flyer may later carry counters or serve as expendable material.
Time this after opponents commit creatures, ideally while protection preserves your countered board or Minsc can rebuild immediately with a fresh Boo.
Cast this before major +1/+1 counter placements when it does not delay Minsc; stack additive enhancers before applying this doubling effect in your calculations.
Play Bill before land drops when possible, spread early counters where they matter, and save the global doubling activation for a board worth the mana.
Use this after blockers or in combination with Fling or Minsc's sacrifice ability so the temporary doubling converts into cards, removal, or lethal damage.
Grow this before combat so its power removes blockers for the entire team; creature entries and counter multipliers can turn a modest setup into broad evasion.

Boo is an excellent Chandra's Ignition source because Ignition clears smaller opposing engines while leaving Boo alive to attack immediately. Sequence the sweep before combat, then send Boo at the opponent whose blockers or value engine were removed.
Use this on a permanent the deck cannot otherwise answer, accepting the uncertain replacement when the current threat is more dangerous than that variance.
Fetch or play this when its basic land types improve fixing; sequence basics first when doing so lets it enter untapped on the critical turn.
Use this as premium untapped color fixing, preserving narrower or painful sources for turns when their special qualities matter.
Use this to secure both the next land drop and the missing color, prioritizing reliable Minsc mana over speculative utility-land development.
Deploy this before chaining green permanents; the life-for-mana option accelerates the turn while each cast broadens the counter payoff across the board.
Use colored mana to make Minsc or another key legendary spell uncounterable; otherwise treat it as an early accelerator rather than a combat body.
Use Domri to accelerate and protect creature-heavy development, then turn a suitably large creature into removal only when the fight is favorable.
Lead with this accelerator when it advances Minsc by a turn, while recognizing that sweep exposure makes the resulting mana temporary.
Recover the card that restores the current plan—protection, a finisher, interaction, or a spent engine—rather than reflexively choosing the highest mana value.
Resolve this before land drops and fetchland activations; proliferate is especially valuable when it grows both creatures and Minsc's loyalty.
Use early as a mana creature, then exploit ferocious for explosive turns; eternalize it after removal when a four-power body and renewed mana matter.
Use the single-target mode to concentrate counters efficiently; overload when a wide creature board justifies six mana, with existing counters increasing rather than enabling the payoff.

With Vorinclex, Monstrous Raider under your control, Fangs of Kalonia compounds twice: the spell's first +1/+1 counter becomes two, and the later placement that doubles the creature's counters is doubled again. For a creature that begins with X +1/+1 counters, the single-target spell leaves it with 3X + 6 counters; sequence Fangs before later fixed counter placements when this multiplication creates decisive damage.
Prioritize Stomping Ground or the land type that fixes the weak color, using the spell to ensure red access without delaying green development.

For lethal calculations, add Fling damage to the combat power that remains after paying its sacrifice cost. A large expendable token is especially valuable when sacrificing it reduces life enough that the surviving attackers still present lethal.

When budgeting a combat-then-Fling line, subtract mandatory attack taxes before declaring the attacker and preserve {1}{R} for Fling. If one intended target taxes combat and another does not, attack the untaxed target and plan to Fling the surviving creature at the taxed target when that ordering preserves both sources of damage.
Treat basic Forest as dependable untapped green development and a resilient target for basic-land search effects.
Let table-wide casting stockpile counters, then redistribute them at upkeep to the attacker, mana engine, or evasive payoff that can use them immediately.
Lead with this accelerator when it advances Minsc by a turn, while recognizing that sweep exposure makes the resulting mana temporary.
Reveal a basic when it preserves tempo, but sequence this tapped on a quiet turn rather than exposing a needed basic solely for speed.
Deploy this before creating or casting four-power creatures so it replaces itself and continues drawing, while trample makes concentrated counters translate into damage.
Cast Ghalta after establishing board power so the discount is substantial; use the large trampler as pressure without abandoning protection for more important engines.
Play this early when several red or green spells will benefit, and sequence multicolored spells to maximize the repeated generic discount.
Deploy before non-Human creatures to seed counters broadly, noting which Humans receive no benefit before planning the curve.
Use this to convert generic mana into both colors, accounting for its activation cost when sequencing a tight multi-spell turn.
Play this when a tapped land does not cost tempo, preferably returning a land with future value or ensuring the next land drop rather than constraining the hand.
Increase their power before combat when possible, then place the resulting counters and haste on the creature that can exploit them immediately.
Cast this cheaply before repeated placements; in counter math, apply this additive increase before the deck's doubling replacements.
Reserve this for interaction that would remove several important permanents or break a decisive line; protecting the whole engine is its premium use.
Advance levels when the board can exploit them, using ward to secure countered permanents and level three to double both creature and loyalty counters.
Hold this to answer a destroy or damage-based sweep affecting countered creatures, or to refill from several such creatures; the best cast accomplishes both.
Cast this after ordinary counter placement but before damage or sacrifice conversion, choosing a threat whose doubled counters create immediate value.
Protect the attack trigger when the board contains several countered creatures; even one attack can turn a distributed setup into lethal pressure.
Deploy before counter placements for the additive bonus, then grow Kami so its variable mana funds a larger follow-up turn.
Use colorless mana when possible and spend life only for needed colors, preserving life without compromising the deck's early tempo.
Use the land face when red development is short; otherwise hold the spell face to convert a large expendable creature into reach or removal.
Use this as late-game mana conversion and trample access, targeting the creature whose safe attack or sacrifice most benefits from the added power.
Establish modified attackers before combat, then spread damage across players when doing so yields multiple basic-land triggers without sacrificing profitable attacks.
Use this to secure both the next land drop and the missing color, prioritizing reliable Minsc mana over speculative utility-land development.
Lead with this accelerator when it advances Minsc by a turn, while recognizing that sweep exposure makes the resulting mana temporary.
Deploy while several players are likely to cast spells, then leverage trample and protection once accumulated counters make it a serious threat.

Treat Boo as recyclable damage and cards. Before spending Minsc's loyalty activation on growth, compare Boo's actual power with visible blockers and the value of a sacrifice conversion. If a large or indestructible blocker would absorb the attack, choose a less defended target, preserve Boo, or convert it instead of growing it into an unprofitable attack. Reserve the activation for postcombat conversion when combat can first deliver useful damage and leave a surviving payload.
Use this filter after another mana source is available; do not count it as a standalone colored source in an opening sequence.
Treat basic Mountain as dependable untapped red development, especially when preserving access to instant-speed power conversion or removal.
Find Stomping Ground or another Forest that supplies the needed color, exploiting untapped entry when the fetched land and life total permit it.
Deploy before counter placements for the additive bonus; use its activated counter only when sorcery-speed mana does not displace a stronger play.
Choose a trampling, high-power creature so excess one-sided damage becomes reach, and cast this before sacrificing or otherwise losing that creature's power.
Use this early to fix the missing basic color and secure durable acceleration toward Minsc and the deck's expensive counter engines.
Play this colorless utility land only when the hand-size benefit is relevant or colored requirements are already secure.
Choose cards when a large non-Human can refill the hand; choose the team pump only when the immediate combat swing is more valuable.

Choose riot separately for every eligible nontoken creature. Prefer the counter when haste will not produce useful mana, combat damage, or an immediate tap ability before the next untap; choose haste only when acting now is worth more than the permanent counter.
Cast this while a large creature is likely to survive through resolution, and plan a useful five-mana-or-less spell to convert the draw into tempo immediately.
Sequence this after two other lands when possible so it supplies either color untapped on the turns the deck begins making larger plays.
Preserve this utility land for a decisive attacker; its activation is expensive enough that colored development normally comes first.
Preserve a Mountain or Forest type in the early sequence so this enters untapped when tempo matters.
Use Ruby as early acceleration, then attack only when a four-power creature safely turns her into meaningful pressure.
Use this as durable fixing and a deterrent, sacrificing at the latest useful moment unless immediate mana development is required.
Deploy this early when the colorless burst advances a real mana threshold, while still planning enough colored sources for the deck's key spells.
In multiplayer this is premium untapped fixing; sequence it early while the opponent-count condition remains reliable.
Fetch this to establish both colors and land types, paying life only when untapped mana materially improves the current or next turn.
Use this to protect a strategically important creature or grant haste for immediate value; avoid exposing it on a low-impact body without a reason.
Exploit changeling by treating this as a Hamster for Minsc's card-draw sacrifice, while opposing spells naturally grow its power.
Arrange a counter placement on each player's turn when feasible, because its once-per-turn draw can turn reactive growth into sustained cards.
Resolve this before green spell chains and major counter events; its cost reduction and doubling reward a developed hand more than an empty board.
Use creature turnover to bank otherwise lost counters, including replacing Boo via the legend rule, then move them onto the best immediate attacker.
Use this as colorless acceleration, with no-maximum-hand-size becoming relevant after Minsc or a large draw spell refills the hand.
Find Stomping Ground or another Forest that supplies the needed color, exploiting untapped entry when the fetched land and life total permit it.
Cast this after other power increases and before damage or sacrifice conversion, since doubling a larger final power creates the greatest swing.
Deploy this when the creature board can attack or defend immediately; its repeated combat doubling rewards trample and discourages attacks throughout the full turn cycle.
Use haste for immediate pressure and sequence it before major counter placements; remember its doubling also magnifies Minsc's loyalty development.
Fetch the color or basic land type the hand lacks, and preserve the shuffle or second landfall event when top-card information or landfall engines make timing valuable.

With Bristly Bill, Spine Sower and Evolution Sage in play, treat a fetchland as two separate landfall batches. In each batch, order Bill's counter-placement trigger to resolve before Evolution Sage's proliferate trigger, then activate the fetch only after the first batch resolves so the fetched land repeats the sequence.
Choose the most consequential attacker at combat, preferably one with trample or a postcombat sacrifice outlet that converts the temporary doubled power.

packages.label: Counter multiplication package
packages.description: Overlapping counter multipliers and counter-preservation engines for Boo and other threats.

notes.text: Use the enters trigger on a consequential artifact, enchantment, or land, then exploit the deathtouch body as a deterrent or Biomancy copy target.
Copy a creature whose enters trigger or size makes every token-fight valuable; Acidic Slime, Terastodon, and Ulvenwald Hydra offer especially strong conversions.
Cast this only when the mana engine is secure and the deck can exploit four cascades; it is also a premium nonlegendary template for March from Velis Vel.
Counter a spell whose impact outweighs the opponent's delayed cards; the light color requirement makes this the interaction easiest to hold through development.
Deploy this early when it advances colored development, but count it as vulnerable acceleration rather than a substitute for a stable land base.
Attack alongside Omo with Courier's trigger ordered below Omo's, allowing a newly placed everything counter to become the kind Courier copies.
Deploy before remaining land drops, then use extra-land effects and fetches to grow the Plant army before exposing it to combat.
Cast Azusa before playing lands for the turn and keep enough lands in hand to use the additional drops rather than treating her as a standalone payoff.
Grow the Gate count before relying on this as an engine; everything counters and Planar Nexus can make its variable output substantial.
Use this before combat to concentrate the Gate count into a decisive attacker, especially a land creature or commander that already has evasion.
Preserve this broad answer for a permanent that materially threatens the plan; the replacement body is usually preferable to leaving an engine or win condition intact.
Develop its charge count toward a troublesome mana value, preserving it as a reset until sacrificing the land is worth more than its mana production.
Use this when colorless utility lands strain fixing; once colors are secure, evaluate it primarily as three-mana acceleration.
Deploy after Spelunking when possible and increase the Locus count with everything counters or copies before planning around its large mana output.
Use this as premium untapped color fixing, preserving narrower or painful sources for turns when their special qualities matter.
Copy the land whose engine or utility is currently most valuable; it enters with copied characteristics, so it does not shortcut Dark Depths' ice counters.
Preserve the double-blue answer for a spell that would win, dismantle the land engine, or invalidate the current development plan.

Do not sacrifice an early land merely because Crop Rotation is available. Once Omo has created extra effective Loci, convert a redundant typed land into Cloudpost for a large mana jump; Ramunap Excavator can later replay the sacrificed land and recover the card economy.
Use this to exile several essential creatures when the 2/2 replacements are strategically irrelevant compared with the engines removed.
Prefer copying this after it is already on the battlefield with Thespian's Stage or Mirage Mirror, creating a zero-counter copy without paying through ten ice counters.
Establish this before sacrificing marked Deserts or utility lands, then build toward five Deserts so its combat trigger becomes a credible board-wide threat.
Sequence this after two other lands so it enters untapped when interaction and development begin competing for mana.
While you control your commander, choose both modes when mana supports it; use the draw as a refill and mill only when it advances a concrete graveyard or finishing plan.
Cast before land drops to gain immediate acceleration, and use universal basic types to solve colors without replacing the deck's nonbasic-type synergies.
Use this early to advance a land from the top five, valuing utility and engine lands when colors are already stable.
Hold this for an opponent's end step when possible, turning spare interaction mana into cards and an extra land before untapping.
Use this as a late defensive reset or to save Omo from commander tax, accepting that it also returns your land-enabling creatures.
Tutor the land that solves the present bottleneck—fixing, engine scale, interaction, or a combo half—rather than following a fixed hierarchy.
Cast for a useful refill when needed, but build toward X at least ten only after extracting value from graveyard cards that would be shuffled back.
Use another green or blue source to filter this into demanding color combinations; do not count it as independent colored mana in an opening hand.
Treat basic Forest as dependable untapped green development and a resilient target for basic-land search effects.
Time this land drop for a meaningful Locus count when practical; it enters untapped, but producing only colorless can still constrain early sequencing.
Hold this through interaction windows when possible, then convert unused mana into a card and an additional land at the latest useful moment.
Mark useful creatures as Merfolk before combat, letting explores improve the board and graveyard while Hakbal turns an attack into land development or a card.
Use this clean refill when the turn can spare sorcery-speed mana, especially after acceleration has emptied the hand.
Count this as a Desert for the engine, using its sacrifice pump only when the immediate combat swing exceeds the value of keeping the land.
Equip a creature whose repeated copies create exceptional triggers; Omo supplies fresh everything counters, while large enters effects can snowball quickly.
Sequence this tapped Cave early, then sacrifice it for discover only when five mana and losing the land are justified by the need for a new play.
Use this as flexible fixing and extra-land deployment, then cash it in when ordinary land recursion—or Desert Warfare while it is a Desert—can recover the sacrificed resource.
Find two lands that complete a specific engine or victory line; establish three Deserts first when the extra Zombie bodies materially improve the cast.
Treat this as a mana sink for the deck's largest production turn, activating monstrosity once X creates a board capable of ending the game.
Scale X for needed cards and life without exhausting interaction; the cast trigger still supplies value even when the creature itself is answered.
Treat basic Island as dependable untapped blue development, especially when preserving mana for interaction or selection.
Use repeated commander casts to enlarge its entry, then increase Jyoti's power before combat so every animated land receives a larger bonus.
Keep this as a land until excess mana and a safe attack make animation worthwhile; avoid exposing mana development to routine creature removal.
Use creatures as fixing only when expendable, and save the Desert-recursion mode for a graveyard creature whose 4/4 copy advances a concrete line.
Place an everything counter on important creatures before deploying this so they become protected Illusions while also receiving the anthem.
Use this hexproof land as resilient late pressure or a protected land-creature payoff, not as an early creature at the expense of development.
Sequence this tapped Desert on a quiet turn; the incidental damage matters less than expanding Desert synergies and supplying both colors.
Deploy when Cloudpost, marked Urza lands, Mana Reflection, or other high-output lands make untapping them net positive mana.
Cast this when enough permanents can produce mana immediately or survive to the next turn, then convert the doubled output into a decisive spell or activation.
Name a nonbasic type shared by marked lands and copy a powerful nonlegendary creature; avoid legendary templates that could sacrifice the animated land army.
Use activations to assemble differently named Gates while tracking the tempo of returning Maze; everything counters help qualify lands but do not change their names.
Keep two mana available to copy the best temporary permanent, with a zero-counter Dark Depths copy offering the deck's cleanest compact finish.
Use scry to improve land and creature access, and commit loyalty to the zero ability only when the known top card and mana-value ceiling justify it.

When Nissa can enter with at least six loyalty, consider using -6 immediately to untap and animate two low-utility lands as 5/5 creatures with flying and haste; two attackers can finish a low-life opponent through a single flying blocker while preserving marked lands and premium fixing.
Spread everything counters across durable, differently named lands and strategically chosen creatures, prioritizing the type identity that unlocks the next engine.

Do not attack with Omo solely to collect everything counters when an untapped blocker can kill the commander while protecting the chosen defender or planeswalker. Treat the attack trigger as secondary to preserving repeated counter access unless losing Omo immediately advances a stronger line.
Cast before using land drops, then play lands from the revealed top whenever possible to clear the deck and preserve hand resources.
Use this filter after another mana source is available; it fixes both colors efficiently but cannot start a mana sequence by itself.
Treat this as a universal nonbasic-type enabler and premium land-tutor target, scaling Gate, Locus, Desert, Cave, and Urza-land payoffs simultaneously.
Spend this efficient answer on a creature whose engine or lethal threat matters far more than the replacement Ape.
Mark creatures as Elves with Omo to enlarge this mana engine, while counting opposing Elves before choosing when to commit it.
Deploy this when wide attacks threaten your setup, using the tax to buy development time rather than assuming it prevents focused pressure entirely.
Cast before extra land drops, then use bounce lands and land recursion to sustain 4/4 production beyond ordinary once-per-turn development.
Value this mainly after eliminations or when combat damage can mill enough lands to create a major development burst; otherwise it is a slow threat.
Use land drops from the graveyard on fetches and sacrificed utility lands, sequencing Excavator before the land play that recovers the most value.
Copy the permanent that best compounds the current engine, and demonstrate only when the political concession is worth granting an opponent a copy.
Build the Gate count before animating lands, then untap Sage with spare Gates to generate mana or multiple threatening land creatures.
Use this to secure a land while stocking Uro and land-recursion resources; accept the self-mill only when those graveyard connections are useful.
Resolve this before land drops and protect the transition past six lands, where each trigger begins multiplying the engine rather than producing isolated bodies.
Use the bounce to guarantee a later landfall trigger or reuse an enters effect, while scheduling its tapped entry on a low-pressure turn.
Preserve this differently named Gate for Maze's End and Gate-count payoffs, sequencing its tapped entry before the critical interaction turn.
Deploy this early when the colorless burst advances a real mana threshold, while still planning enough colored sources for the deck's key spells.
Cast before lands or land tutors that would make lands enter tapped so they enter untapped instead; the replacement card makes this an efficient setup play.
Reserve this for a dangerous stack containing abilities or multiple spells that ordinary countermagic cannot cleanly answer.
Protect graveyard resources until copying a high-impact spell or ability is worth exiling seven cards, especially a tutor, draw spell, or Maze activation.
Find the land that solves the current bottleneck or completes a known package, weighing the tempo of putting it in hand rather than directly onto the battlefield.
Keep this in hand when instant-speed phasing can protect or neutralize a creature; otherwise deploy it as a Gate and fixing source when development requires it.
Resolve Tatyova before land drops, then chain extra lands and recursion to convert development into both cards and stabilization.
Use the scry to find the next land-engine piece or interaction, sequencing the tapped land when it does not compromise a response window.
Choose up to three noncreature permanents whose removal justifies giving away 3/3 bodies; copying or recurring the enters trigger can dominate resource engines.
Copy the best land engine at low opportunity cost, or copy an established Dark Depths to create the zero-counter version needed for Marit Lage.
Scale the Locus count before using this as a mill outlet, and target milling only when it advances a graveyard plan or provides a realistic finish.
Use the enters trigger to fetch the exact utility or combo land needed, then leverage its land-scaled body for defense, Biomancy, or combat.
Cast before the turn's final land drop so the extra-play permission is usable, turning the three-card refill into immediate development.
Use early entries for cards, life, and land drops, then manage the graveyard so escape does not consume lands or pieces needed by other engines.
Hold this as a land tutor when a specific utility land is worth four mana and sacrificing a land; recursion can soften that card cost.
Combine this with printed or everything-enabled Urza subtypes; prioritize complete type support before treating it as more than colorless development.
Combine this with printed or everything-enabled Urza subtypes; prioritize complete type support before treating it as more than colorless development.
Combine this with printed or everything-enabled Urza subtypes; once enabled, its larger output makes it the most valuable member to untap or copy.

Copy the land whose static or enters value best advances the engine; when it enters as Dark Depths, the copied 'enters with' replacement puts ten ice counters on it—counters themselves are never copied.
Reveal a basic when convenient to preserve tempo, but do not weaken the overall land sequence merely to force untapped entry.
Use this to answer an exceptional nonbasic land and create Treasure, preferably when ordinary land recursion—or Desert Warfare while it is a Desert—can recover Volatile Fault.
Use this reset while Omo remains present so marked nonland creatures count as Serpents and stay, creating a potentially asymmetric tempo swing.
Return a marked or naturally nonbasic-typed land to avoid discarding, creating both card selection and another future landfall trigger.
Spread flood counters onto high-output lands and other permanents with counters, then exploit the end-step untap as a second mana or activation window.
Use colorless mana when possible and pay life only for required colors, balancing early tempo against long-game life preservation.
Use universal Forest typing to fix green and enable land interactions, but consider that opponents receive the same benefit before deploying it.

notes.text: Use colorless mana when possible and spend life only for required white or blue, preserving tempo without paying unnecessary life.
Treat Alseid as both an enchantment trigger and held protection; sacrifice it only when the chosen color actually preserves a key creature or enchantment line.
Use the plus ability to stage a miracle, the blink to reuse a high-value permanent, and preserve her when Felidar Guardian can form a repeatable engine.

Preserve Aminatou when the next turn depends on her miracle engine, but survival takes priority. Before declining a block, count both incoming combat damage and visible follow-up damage or sacrifice conversions; accept losing the commander when preserving her would leave you facing lethal. If blocking is safe to decline, compare the next enchantment's normal cost with available mana before exposing her, and retain her when the commander-dependent line is still realistically reachable.
Select a creature whose immediate enters value or recursion connectivity outweighs the Aura's fragility, and exploit each enchantment entry the cast creates.
Deploy this early when it advances colored development, but count it as vulnerable acceleration rather than a substitute for a stable land base.
Use this primarily to fetch a white-producing typed land, timing the shuffle when top-card setup from tutors or selection makes it relevant.
Deploy this early to replace itself and deter attacks; later it is excellent disposable material for sacrifice and reanimation loops.
Use this to fetch a black-producing typed land, preserving the shuffle until after top-card information when practical.
Copy the creature that supplies the missing recursion or payoff role, especially a Lark, Guide, Titan, or enters-trigger piece that connects several zones.
Use this to place a desired miracle enchantment on top and a disposable card beneath it, while preserving a shuffle effect to clear unwanted cards.
Use colorless mana when possible and spend life only for required white or black, preserving tempo without paying unnecessary life.
Use flash and replicate to turn impending deaths into permanent control swings; recursive sacrifice lines can repeatedly exploit its return trigger.

When an opponent casts Uro without escaping it, flash in Changing Loyalty after Uro's mandatory sacrifice trigger is on the stack. Uro's impending death then triggers the Aura to return it under your control, producing another enter-the-battlefield sequence before the returned non-escaped Uro sacrifices itself again.
Treat this as a repeatable exchange engine: sacrifice low-value bodies for connected graveyard creatures while each recast retriggers enchantment payoffs.
Use this premium fixing when exact colors matter, but avoid needless taps that convert harmless sequencing into avoidable life loss.
Use this as premium untapped color fixing, preserving narrower or painful sources for turns when their special qualities matter.
Cast this when selection matters or mana would otherwise go unused, placing a useful recursion target in the graveyard while preserving needed top cards.
Reanimate a target worth the tapped-entry and upkeep friction, prioritizing an enters trigger or combo link that functions even before attacking.
Sequence this after two other lands when possible so it supplies white or blue untapped during turns with competing actions.
Transmute this for the four-mana card that best links the plan, or retain it as a repeatable sacrifice outlet when recursion pieces are already assembled.
Resolve this before chaining enchantments so each entry weakens opposing boards; repeated Aura and Nightmare entries can turn it into a controlled sweep.
Keep this as an untapped white source unless channeling it efficiently removes an attacker or blocker without compromising the mana base.
Choose a consequential permanent for chapter I; use chapter II's tax through the intervening turn cycle, then plan chapter III knowing that tax expires before the reanimation trigger.

Because this is an instant, default to the latest safe opponent end step rather than casting in a main phase. Use the intervening turns to identify the actual missing engine role and opponents' threats; take an earlier window only when the immediate draw, mana, or protection payoff materially outweighs that information.

Before tutoring in upkeep, count both the tutor mana and the replaced draw against the next main phase. Do not fetch a long-term engine if casting the tutor delays the mana development needed to deploy it or leaves the deck exposed to current pressure.

On the controller's own turn, flashing Entity Tracker in during the draw step can establish the enchantment engine before the main phase without consuming a main action. A cheap reanimation Aura can then trigger Tracker while returning a creature with its own enters-the-battlefield value.
Use this as low-cost fixing after confirming opponents' lands provide the needed color; do not assume all three colors are always available.
Use this as an enchantment trigger and free sacrifice outlet, concentrating temporary power on an evasive creature only when it advances a finishing or recursion line.
Preserve disposable creatures as free sacrifice currency, using regeneration to protect a key body while enabling Lark-style recursion loops.
Blink the permanent with the strongest reusable enters or loyalty value, and recognize Aminatou the Fateshifter as a repeatable loop partner.

Treat Felidar Guardian as a Reveillark recovery bridge as well as a generic blink piece. If Karmic Guide and a free sacrifice outlet such as Viscera Seer are in the graveyard while Reveillark is on the battlefield, blink Reveillark so its leave trigger returns Guide plus the outlet. With Alseid of Life's Bounty and Grim Guardian available, establish Grim Guardian, then repeatedly sacrifice Alseid, Guide, and Reveillark: Lark returns Guide plus Alseid, Guide returns Lark, and Alseid's enchantment entry drains every opponent.
Use this for early acceleration when opponents supply the needed color, but verify its live colors before planning a tightly colored follow-up.
Reserve the free counter for a noncreature spell that breaks the engine or enables an opponent's win, keeping the commander present when possible.
Fetch the typed land that fixes white or blue, and time the shuffle after Top, Brainstorm, or a tutor has exposed unwanted cards.
Deploy Funeral Room before death loops for a drain payload, or use Ghostly Dancers to unlock Awakening Hall when mass reanimation will create a decisive turn.
Recover an enchantment or shortcut Awakening Hall on entry, then chain enchantments to produce evasive bodies that can fuel sacrifice and recursion.
Construct piles where every opponent choice advances the plan; requesting only two cards can deliberately place both into the graveyard for reanimation.
Use opponents' second draws to build Treasure, and activate the symmetrical draw only when the selected ally or political exchange benefits you more.

Remember the clever line of reanimating Glen Elendra Archmage at instant speed in response to a noncreature spell. Once Glen enters and priority reaches you again, pay {U} and sacrifice it to counter that spell.
Fetch this when white and black access outweigh two life, choosing tapped entry whenever immediate mana does not materially change the turn.
Tutor the creature or card that the graveyard engine currently lacks, then exploit Lamia's enchantment entry, lifelink, and graveyard-casting discount.

Before choosing Lamia's graveyard tutor target, inventory the current sacrifice outlet, recursion bodies, eligible power-two-or-less targets, and payoff. Prefer the target that completes a live deterministic or self-rebuilding Lark line over generic reanimation value; for example, with Karmic Guide, Fanatical Devotion, and Grim Guardian already positioned, put Reveillark into the graveyard.
Establish this before repeated enchantment entries or recursion loops so each cycle becomes table-wide damage and a potential deterministic finish.

Use this at the preceding end step to stage a miracle enchantment or recover a key engine, accounting for the draw it replaces. Weigh recursion with this card against value of new unknown draws. Best held until end of turn of last player before you.
Fetch this when white and blue access outweigh two life, choosing tapped entry whenever immediate mana does not materially change the turn.
Tutor the Aura that supplies the missing recursion or removal role, then defeat the battle only when Ephara's enchantment-draw engine is worth the combat.
Treat basic Island as dependable untapped blue development, especially when preserving mana for interaction or selection.
Return the creature that reconnects the recursion chain, valuing Guide's enters trigger even when echo will make the body temporary.
Use this as ordinary interaction or pair its leaves trigger with reanimation Auras and sacrifice outlets to create repeatable enchantment movement.

Preserve Liliana's untapped protection ability through the opposing turn cycle when an important creature may need shielding. Do not attack merely because protection is unnecessary at the current moment.
Remove a meaningful artifact or enchantment on entry, and offer the shared draw only when the political or card-flow exchange favors your position.
Use this perfect fixing for demanding turns and avoid tapping it for colors another source could provide without life loss.
Fetch the typed land that fixes white or black, and time the shuffle after top-card setup when possible.
Use this as early colorless acceleration, then cash it in once mana is plentiful or recursion can profitably recover the artifact.
Use this primarily to fetch a blue-producing typed land, preserving the shuffle for Top or Brainstorm cleanup when practical.
Use this as premium untapped blue-black fixing while the multiplayer condition is secure, especially for holding interaction.
Evoke when two cards matter more than the body, or reanimate and blink it repeatedly when a persistent value creature better serves the engine.
Deploy this early enough to tax a spell-heavy table, then stop paying cumulative upkeep once the mana burden displaces stronger development.
Use normal timing for a durable reanimation Aura or flash it as interaction or combo assembly when the temporary cleanup sacrifice is acceptable.
Exile a permanent that materially blocks the plan, while recognizing that sacrifice or blink interactions can manipulate its linked triggers.
Use flash to spend otherwise idle mana, but account for its mandatory draw; treat it as miracle access only for the turn's first draw while Aminatou, Veil Piercer is present.
Use this inexpensive selection in a response window, but remember it draws the kept top card; consume a staged enchantment only as the turn's first draw with Aminatou, Veil Piercer present.
Preserve this as an untapped blue source unless channeling it solves a crucial permanent at instant speed without exposing the spell to counters.

When removal targets Parallax Wave on an otherwise empty stack, desired Wave activations can be stacked above that removal so they resolve and become linked before Wave leaves. Conversely, removal placed above a Wave activation can make that pending activation resolve after Wave has left, so check the full stack before committing targets.

When Parallax Wave has fade counters available, consider preserving its instant-speed creature exile as a publicly visible deterrent and use table talk to make that defensive capacity salient without revealing hidden information. This is especially useful against an enlarged Boo, which can be exiled before combat damage or sacrifice conversion; spend the counters instead when a combo, protective blink, or higher-value control sequence outweighs the deterrence.
Treat basic Plains as dependable untapped white development and a resilient target for basic-land search effects.
Fetch the typed land that fixes blue or black, and time the shuffle after Top, Brainstorm, or a tutor has exposed unwanted cards.
Sequence this tapped tri-land early for complete fixing, or cycle it later when colors are secure and a fresh card is more valuable.
Use this as tempo against an expensive or timing-sensitive spell, or protect your own spell from opposing interaction while replacing Remand with a card.
Build the graveyard before committing this mass-recursion spell, aiming to return an interconnected enchantment engine rather than isolated value pieces.
Preserve this as a blocker, evoke trigger, or combo hinge; its leave trigger should return the pair of small creatures that creates the strongest connected line.

Against a single attacker that can kill them together, treat Reveillark and Mulldrifter as a proactive recursion block rather than preserving them for incidental attacks. If Karmic Guide is already in the graveyard, let Lark and Mulldrifter die, return both with Lark's leave trigger, then use Karmic's enter trigger to return Lark. If Guide is on the battlefield and must be recycled too, include it in the block or a simultaneous sacrifice exchange before Lark's trigger resolves.
Deploy this before a spell-heavy turn cycle and track optional draws carefully when the top card has been staged for Aminatou's miracle window.
Use this primarily to fetch a blue-producing typed land, preserving the shuffle for top-card cleanup when practical.
Use this as premium untapped white-blue fixing while the multiplayer condition is secure, especially for holding interaction.

With Aminatou in play, activate Top at the preceding end step and arrange the desired miracle enchantment first with a disposable card second. Aminatou can surveil the second card into the graveyard while leaving the miracle card on top for the draw step. Be careful when planning with this card - cracking a fetch land will shuffle your deck and the card will be lost. But, by the same token, cracking a fetch can shuffle away unwanted draws identified with this card.
Sequence this after two other lands so it supplies white or black untapped when engines and interaction begin competing for mana.
Sequence this after two other lands so it supplies blue or black untapped when engines and interaction begin competing for mana.
Use this as colored development early, then convert it into a card when mana is abundant or land recursion can recover the loss.
Deploy before draw-heavy turn cycles, then convert Treasure into a protected engine or multi-spell turn rather than spending it without a plan.
Deploy this early when the colorless burst advances a real mana threshold, while still planning enough colored sources for the deck's key spells.
Use this as an enchantment entry, replacement card, and disposable body; repeated recursion turns the modest enters trigger into reliable engine fuel.
Recover a high-impact enchantment each upkeep, but track the five-enchantment threshold because animating the board can expose engines to creature removal or enable loops.

At five or more enchantments, Starfield animates Parallax Wave and enables Wave to target itself. Stack other creature-exile activations below the self-exile activation; Wave leaves first, then returns itself and its linked cards with fresh fade counters. With Grim Guardian present, repeating the reset produces table-wide life loss and a deterministic finish, so preserve the three-piece line and check for opposing interaction before committing.
Return the low-cost permanent that restores the most engine connectivity, and seek safe attacks or blink loops to repeat that recursion.
Treat basic Swamp as dependable untapped black development and a resilient target for basic-land search effects.
Reserve this efficient counter for an enchantment, instant, or sorcery that threatens a win or disrupts the engine; the Bird is usually an acceptable concession.
Use colorless mana when available and pay life only for needed blue or black, accelerating toward Aminatou without losing color discipline.
Use colorless mana when available and pay life only for needed white or black, accelerating toward Aminatou without losing color discipline.
Use colorless mana when available and pay life only for needed white or blue, accelerating toward Aminatou without losing color discipline.
Read ahead to the chapter the position needs: tutor for setup, reanimate for immediate impact, or begin at disruption when the full Saga sequence is valuable.
Choose X to reshape the board without discarding useful survivors, then exploit later death loops as drain and opposing deaths as stabilization.
Use chapter two to discard a recursion target and recover a cheap permanent, then leverage the transformed body's token production as sacrifice material.
Cast it as an enchantment for durable removal and triggers, or channel it to blink a valuable creature or temporarily clear a threat at instant speed.
Deploy before enchantment chains for stabilization, then use the drain activation only when excess mana or a finishing loop makes the life payment worthwhile.
Develop its Construct only when artifacts support it, then tutor Top or Sol Ring; recursion can replay the Saga and repeat the entire value sequence.
Use this near the draw that will consume it, finding the exact missing engine or answer and accounting for both the life cost and lost natural draw.
Use this as premium untapped white-black fixing while the multiplayer condition is secure.
Use this primarily to fetch a black-producing typed land, preserving the shuffle for top-card cleanup when practical.
Use evoke or sacrifice to recover a one-power combo or value creature, with Body Double and Viscera Seer making it an important recursion hinge.
Plan three enchantment entries in one turn when possible, sequencing surveil, discard, and reanimation so each escalating eerie resolution advances the line.
Treat this as free sacrifice infrastructure and repeatable top-card selection, using each death to advance recursion while arranging or clearing miracle draws.
Fetch this when blue and black access outweigh two life, choosing tapped entry whenever immediate mana does not materially change the turn.
Use this primarily to fetch a white-producing typed land, preserving the shuffle for top-card cleanup when practical.
